374	def _validate_route_walk(
375	    grid: GridMap,
376	    origin: Position,
377	    route: Sequence[object],
378	    *,
379	    robot_id: str,
380	    checkpoint: bool,
381	    blocked_cells: frozenset[Position] | None = None,
382	) -> list[Position]:
383	    """Validate one robot's remaining route as a cell-by-cell map walk.
384	
385	    This is the single place that owns the walking rule shared by direct
386	    fleet construction and checkpoint recovery, so the same legality check is
387	    never edited twice. A route holds the cells still ahead of *origin*:
388	
389	    * every waypoint must parse as two plain integers (booleans are rejected),
390	      and lie inside the map -- a cell in *blocked_cells* is the one kind of
391	      currently obstructed waypoint a version 2 checkpoint recovery may carry
392	      (see below), everything else off the traversable map is rejected;
393	    * the first waypoint must be an up/down/left/right neighbour of *origin*,
394	      so a first waypoint equal to the current cell is rejected;
395	    * every later waypoint must be exactly one orthogonal step from the
396	      previous one -- diagonal moves, multi-cell jumps and two identical
397	      consecutive waypoints are all rejected.
398	
399	    Detours and revisits (including *origin*) are legal, and a route crossing
400	    another robot's cell is never a walk error: traffic is settled while
401	    stepping, not here. The walkability rule deliberately says nothing about
402	    the bound task's pickup/dropoff requirements; checkpoint loading keeps
403	    that separate, stricter business check. The result is a fresh mutable list
404	    of tuple cells, so validating never aliases or mutates the caller's
405	    container and a rejected input leaves every earlier object untouched.
406	
407	    *blocked_cells* is honoured only for checkpoint recovery and names the
408	    cells the recorded map-change history explains: cells open on the base map
409	    that an accepted edit has since closed and that are still closed at save
410	    time. A taskless robot's preset route may legitimately end on such a cell
411	    -- the robot keeps its unconsumed waypoints and simply waits before it --
412	    so those waypoints walk as well as the open cells do. The exemption is
413	    deliberately narrow: only checkpoint loading ever supplies the set (direct
414	    construction leaves it ``None``), only a robot without a bound task may
415	    use it (the caller never passes the set for a task route), and the cells
416	    must be inside the map -- an out-of-bounds waypoint is rejected regardless.
417	    A blocked cell in the base map that no edit explains is never part of the
418	    set, so a route crossing an initial or unexplained obstacle stays illegal.
419	
420	    The two entries keep their existing format and wording differences via
421	    *checkpoint*: direct construction (false) accepts a list or tuple route of
422	    list-or-tuple cells and reports ``route waypoint N`` with a dedicated
423	    message for a first waypoint on the current cell and for repeated
424	    consecutive waypoints; checkpoint loading (true) keeps the strict JSON
425	    list-of-lists format (``_as_pair``), says ``route entry`` and folds both
426	    equal-cell cases into its existing non-adjacency message. The checks
427	    performed are identical either way.
428	    """
429	    allowed_blocked = frozenset() if blocked_cells is None else blocked_cells
430	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
431	    previous = origin
432	    for index, cell in enumerate(route):
433	        if checkpoint:
434	            waypoint = _as_pair(
435	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {index}"
436	            )
437	        else:
438	            waypoint = _as_cell(
439	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index}"
440	            )
441	        if not grid.contains(waypoint) or (
442	            waypoint in grid.obstacles and waypoint not in allowed_blocked
443	        ):
444	            if checkpoint:
445	                raise ValueError(
446	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
447	                    "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
448	                )
449	            raise ValueError(
450	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index} "
451	                f"{list(waypoint)} is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
452	            )
453	        if waypoint == previous:
454	            if checkpoint:
455	                # The checkpoint wording treats an equal cell like any other
456	                # non-adjacent step, naming both cells of the offending move.
457	                raise ValueError(
458	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
459	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
460	                )
461	            if index == 0:
462	                raise ValueError(
463	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)} "
464	                    "is the robot's current cell; the remaining route must "
465	                    "start with the next cell"
466	                )
467	            raise ValueError(
468	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route repeats cell {list(waypoint)} at "
469	                f"consecutive waypoints {index - 1} and {index}"
470	            )
471	        if (
472	            abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0])
473	            + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1])
474	            != 1
475	        ):
476	            if checkpoint:
477	                raise ValueError(
478	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
479	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
480	                )
481	            if index == 0:
482	                segment = (
483	                    f"from its current position {list(previous)} to route "
484	                    f"waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)}"
485	                )
486	            else:
487	                segment = (
488	                    f"from route waypoint {index - 1} {list(previous)} to "
489	                    f"waypoint {index} {list(waypoint)}"
490	                )
491	            raise ValueError(
492	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently {segment}: "
493	                "every step must move one orthogonal cell"
494	            )
495	        waypoints.append(waypoint)
496	        previous = waypoint
497	    return waypoints

525	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
526	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):
527	            raise ValueError("robot starts outside traversable map space")
528	        self._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
529	        if _routes_prevalidated:

531	            # :func:`_validate_route_walk` itself -- including its one narrow
532	            # checkpoint exemption for a taskless preset route waiting before
533	            # a history-explained closed cell -- so its already-normalized
534	            # routes must not be re-checked here against the saved grid, where
535	            # those legitimate waypoints look obstructed. Every other
536	            # constructor check above still runs.
537	            return

539	        # spelled them: a mutable list of tuple cells. The normalized copies are
540	        # committed only after every robot passed validation, so a rejection
541	        # (even one buried in a later robot's route) never touches the caller's
542	        # objects. See :meth:`_normalize_initial_routes`.

547	    @staticmethod
548	    def _validate_task_ownership(robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]) -> None:
549	        """Reject impossible initial bindings between robots and tasks.
550	
551	        The very same ownership requirements back direct construction and
552	        checkpoint loading, so they live in exactly one place. The mutual
553	        binding only governs work still in progress:
554	
555	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
556	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
557	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
558	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
559	          collected additionally must have an owner.
560	        * A robot can therefore never be claimed by two unfinished tasks: the
561	          second task's owner points at a robot that executes another task.
562	        * A completed task must carry the picked-up mark *and* a historical
563	          owner (a non-null ``assigned_robot``); see below.
564	
565	        Completed tasks are history, not work in progress, but the history must
566	        still be coherent: a finished task must carry both the picked-up mark
567	        and the id of the robot that finished it -- ``None`` means "no record",
568	        never an anonymous completion, even when the pickup point and the
569	        dropoff coincide. Neither gap is repaired (the owner is not filled in,
570	        the pickup mark is not flipped, nothing is reassigned or dropped); the
571	        fleet is rejected as a whole with a :class:`ValueError` naming the task
572	        and the exact contradiction. The historical owner itself is bound by
573	        none of the in-progress rules: it need not be idle or name the task
574	        back, may already work a new task, may have finished several tasks, and
575	        may even be absent from the fleet, so historical records never occupy a
576	        robot or take part in new task assignment. Unassigned, not-yet-collected
577	        tasks simply wait -- even when no robot can reach them -- and are not an
578	        ownership error. Nothing here rewrites a binding or drops a task; an
579	        inconsistent input is rejected as a whole, leaving the caller's objects
580	        untouched.
581	        """
582	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
583	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
584	        for robot in robots:
585	            if robot.task_id is None:
586	                continue
587	            task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
588	            if task is None:
589	                raise ValueError(
590	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task "
591	                    f"{robot.task_id!r}"
592	                )
593	            if task.completed:
594	                raise ValueError(
595	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
596	                    "that is already completed"
597	                )
598	            if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
599	                raise ValueError(
600	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
601	                    f"but the task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
602	                )
603	        for task in tasks:
604	            if task.completed:
605	                # A finished task is a fixed historical record: the goods must
606	                # have been collected and a historical finishing robot must be
607	                # named. The very same requirement backs direct construction
608	                # and checkpoint recovery, so a document that could never be
609	                # loaded again can never be built in the first place. This is
610	                # judged purely from the record -- even a task whose pickup
611	                # point equals its dropoff is not presumed collected -- and the
612	                # recorded robot is history only: it is never looked up, so it
613	                # may be retired, idle or already busy with another task, and
614	                # several completed tasks may name the same robot without ever
615	                # counting as occupying it.
616	                if not task.picked_up:
617	                    if task.assigned_robot is None:
618	                        raise ValueError(
619	                            f"task {task.task_id!r} is marked completed but was "
620	                            "never picked up and has no historical assigned robot"
621	                        )
622	                    raise ValueError(
623	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is marked completed but never "
624	                        "picked up, even though historical robot "
625	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r} is recorded for it"
626	                    )
627	                if task.assigned_robot is None:
628	                    raise ValueError(
629	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is marked completed and picked up "
630	                        "but has no historical assigned robot"
631	                    )
632	                continue
633	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
634	                raise ValueError(
635	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
636	                )
637	            if task.assigned_robot is not None:
638	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
639	                if owner is None:
640	                    raise ValueError(
641	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
642	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
643	                    )
644	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
645	                    raise ValueError(
646	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} "
647	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
648	                    )

650	    @staticmethod
651	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
652	        grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]
653	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
654	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
655	
656	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound, via the single shared walk
657	        validator :func:`_validate_route_walk` -- the same coordinate shape,
658	        map-walkability and one-orthogonal-step rule checkpoint recovery uses
659	        -- so a walking rule never has to be changed in two places. The outer
660	        route may be a list or tuple and each waypoint may itself be a list or
661	        tuple of two plain integers -- booleans are not integers here, and
662	        wrong lengths or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of
663	        leaking unpacking or hashing failures. The forms may be mixed freely;
664	        only the coordinate order matters, not the container types.
665	
666	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
667	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
668	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
669	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
670	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
671	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
672	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
673	
674	        The check is read-only -- :func:`_validate_route_walk` builds fresh
675	        lists, and the caller commits them itself only once every robot has
676	        passed, so a rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a
677	        later robot or at the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders
678	        or otherwise modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. The
679	        shared walk check says nothing about tasks; direct construction keeps
680	        accepting any walkable route, while checkpoint loading keeps its own
681	        stricter validation that also covers the pickup/dropoff rules.
682	        """
683	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
684	        for robot in robots:
685	            route = robot.route
686	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
687	                raise ValueError(
688	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
689	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
690	                )
691	            normalized.append(
692	                _validate_route_walk(
693	                    grid,
694	                    robot.position,
695	                    route,
696	                    robot_id=robot.robot_id,
697	                    checkpoint=False,
698	                )
699	            )
700	        return normalized

706	    def modify_obstacles(
707	        self,
708	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
709	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
710	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
711	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
712	
713	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
714	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
715	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
716	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
717	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
718	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
719	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
720	
721	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
722	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
723	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
724	        distance is accumulated.
725	        """
726	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
727	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
728	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
729	        if conflict:
730	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
731	            raise ValueError(
732	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
733	            )
734	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
735	        for cell in add_cells:
736	            if cell in occupied:
737	                raise ValueError(
738	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
739	                )
740	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)

742	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
743	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
744	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
745	        seen: set[Position] = set()
746	        ordered: list[Position] = []
747	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
748	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
749	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
750	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
751	            if position in seen:
752	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
753	                continue
754	            seen.add(position)
755	            ordered.append(position)
756	        return ordered

758	    def _apply_map_change(
759	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
760	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
761	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
762	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
763	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
764	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
765	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
766	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
767	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
768	
769	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
770	        # known to change the map.
771	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
772	        self._map_sequence += 1
773	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
774	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
775	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
776	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
777	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
778	        return copy.deepcopy(record)

781	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
782	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
783	        return {
784	            "type": "map_change",
785	            "tick": self.tick,
786	            "sequence": sequence,
787	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
788	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
789	        }

791	    def _plan_route(
792	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
793	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
794	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
795	
796	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
797	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
798	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
799	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
800	        """
801	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
802	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)

804	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
805	        for task in self.tasks.values():
806	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
807	                continue
808	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
809	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
810	                continue
811	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
812	            if route is None:
813	                robot.route = []
814	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
815	            else:
816	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
817	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
818	                robot.route = route
819	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)

821	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
822	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
823	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
824	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
825	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
826	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
827	                continue
828	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
829	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
830	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
831	                continue
832	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
833	            if route is None:
834	                robot.route = []
835	                continue
836	            robot.route = route
837	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
838	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

852	    def _safe_side_cells(
853	        self,
854	        robot: Robot,
855	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
856	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
857	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
858	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
859	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
860	
861	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
862	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
863	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
864	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
865	
866	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
867	          skips anything else),
868	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
869	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
870	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
871	          route is excluded), and
872	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
873	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
874	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
875	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
876	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
877	
878	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
879	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
880	        """
881	        blocked = set(forbidden)
882	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
883	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
884	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
885	                continue
886	            yield cell

890	        blocker: Robot,
891	        requester: Robot,
892	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
893	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
894	    ) -> Position | None:
895	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
896	
897	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
898	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
899	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
900	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
901	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
902	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
903	        """
904	        return next(
905	            self._safe_side_cells(
906	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
907	            ),
908	            None,
909	        )

911	    def _self_sidestep(
912	        self,
913	        robot: Robot,
914	        task: Task | None,
915	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
916	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
917	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
918	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
919	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
920	
921	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
922	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
923	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
924	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
925	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
926	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
927	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
928	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
929	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
930	        """
931	        if task is None or task.completed:
932	            return None
933	        destination = robot.route[0]
934	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
935	        if blocker_id is None:
936	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
937	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
938	        best_length = 0
939	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
940	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
941	        # that order as the tie break.
942	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
943	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
944	            if route is None:
945	                continue
946	            if (
947	                blocker_id is not None
948	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
949	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
950	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
951	                )
952	            ):
953	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
954	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
955	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
956	                continue
957	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
958	                best = (cell, route)
959	                best_length = len(route)
960	        return best

962	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
963	        self,
964	        robot: Robot,
965	        side: Position,
966	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
967	        blocker_id: str,
968	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
969	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
970	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
971	    ) -> bool:
972	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
973	
974	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
975	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
976	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
977	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
978	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
979	        never rejected here.
980	        """
981	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
982	            return False
983	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
984	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
985	            return False
986	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
987	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
988	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
989	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
990	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
991	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
992	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
993	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
994	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
995	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
996	        return not self._can_vacate(
997	            blocker,
998	            robot,
999	            hyp_occupied,
1000	            reserved,
1001	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
1002	            blocked_path,
1003	        )

1005	    def _side_exit_cells(
1006	        self,
1007	        robot: Robot,
1008	        task: Task,
1009	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1010	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1011	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
1012	    ) -> Iterator[tuple[Position, list[Position]]]:
1013	        """Side cells a busy robot could escape to, with their replanned routes.
1014	
1015	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route that keep the robot's
1016	        task reachable are offered, in deterministic neighbour order. Whether
1017	        such a cell is a genuine way out -- or just moves the robot aside for
1018	        one tick before it is driven back onto the same blocked corridor -- is
1019	        judged by the caller as it scans the candidates.
1020	        """
1021	        for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
1022	            robot, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
1023	        ):
1024	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=side_cell)
1025	            if route is not None:
1026	                yield side_cell, route

1028	    def _can_vacate(
1029	        self,
1030	        blocker: Robot,
1031	        requester: Robot,
1032	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
1033	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
1034	        checking: frozenset[str],
1035	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
1036	    ) -> bool:
1037	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
1038	
1039	        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
1040	        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
1041	        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
1042	        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
1043	        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
1044	        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
1045	        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots already on the
1046	        dependency chain (including robots that used their one move of this
1047	        tick), so meeting one again closes a cyclic dependency -- a head-on
1048	        deadlock, or the requester itself -- and never proves an exit merely
1049	        because every robot on the cycle still carries a route.
1050	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
1051	        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
1052	        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
1053	        the blocker's own route does).
1054	
1055	        A task-bound blocker's own side step is judged by the same standard as
1056	        the requester's retreat: it counts as leaving only when the replanned
1057	        route from the side cell does not lead straight back through the cell
1058	        being vacated into another robot that cannot get out of the way
1059	        either. A side cell the blocker must leave again on the next tick to
1060	        re-face the very same unyielding jam further down the corridor is no
1061	        way out, so it never justifies the retreat behind it.
1062	
1063	        The follow chain can run through an arbitrarily long legal queue, so
1064	        the search is an explicit stack rather than Python recursion: a queue
1065	        of twelve hundred robots ending at a parked robot with no side cell
1066	        must report "cannot vacate" from a normal ``step()`` instead of
1067	        raising :class:`RecursionError`. Each frame is
1068	        ``(robot, occupied, checking, blocked_path, resume)``: a nested
1069	        hypothetical (the blocker having stepped aside) works with its own
1070	        layout and no-go cells, so both travel with the frame. *resume* is
1071	        ``None`` on a frame's first visit and afterwards holds the robot's
1072	        not-yet-tried side-exit candidates as a stateful iterator. A frame
1073	        examined for the first time first tries the free-waypoint and
1074	        follow-chain rules; only when the chain ahead comes back empty does it
1075	        resume at its own side-cell scan, continuing exactly where that scan
1076	        stopped -- the order the single recursive call imposed.
1077	        """
1078	        frame = (blocker, occupied, checking, blocked_path, None)
1079	        stack: list[
1080	            tuple[
1081	                Robot,
1082	                dict[Position, str],
1083	                frozenset[str],
1084	                frozenset[Position],
1085	                Iterator[tuple[Position, list[Position]]] | None,
1086	            ]
1087	        ] = [frame]
1088	        while stack:
1089	            current, cur_occupied, cur_checking, cur_blocked_path, resume = stack.pop()
1090	            if current.robot_id in cur_checking:
1091	                # The chain has folded back onto a robot it already depends
1092	                # on: a cycle cannot vacate itself. The frame that followed
1093	                # this one simply resumes with its own side-cell options.
1094	                continue
1095	            task = self.tasks[current.task_id] if current.task_id is not None else None
1096	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1097	                continue
1098	            if not current.route:
1099	                if task is not None:
1100	                    # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this
1101	                    # tick; it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
1102	                    continue
1103	                # A parked robot (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
1104	                # yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; it does
1105	                # so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
1106	                # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
1107	                # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
1108	                # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
1109	                side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(current, requester, cur_occupied, reserved)
1110	                if side is not None and side not in cur_blocked_path:
1111	                    return True
1112	                continue
1113	            if resume is None:
1114	                ahead = current.route[0]
1115	                if (
1116	                    self.grid.traversable(ahead)
1117	                    and ahead not in cur_occupied
1118	                    and ahead not in reserved
1119	                ):
1120	                    return True
1121	                occupant_id = cur_occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
1122	                if (
1123	                    occupant_id is not None
1124	                    and occupant_id != current.robot_id
1125	                    and occupant_id not in cur_checking
1126	                ):
1127	                    # The robot could follow the occupant once that robot
1128	                    # vacates its cell this same tick. This frame resumes with
1129	                    # its side-cell scan only after the chain ahead proves it
1130	                    # cannot clear, mirroring the recursive call order.
1131	                    stack.append(
1132	                        (
1133	                            current,
1134	                            cur_occupied,
1135	                            cur_checking,
1136	                            cur_blocked_path,
1137	                            self._side_exit_cells(
1138	                                current, task, cur_occupied, reserved, cur_blocked_path
1139	                            )
1140	                            if task is not None
1141	                            else iter(()),
1142	                        )
1143	                    )
1144	                    stack.append(
1145	                        (
1146	                            self.robots[occupant_id],
1147	                            cur_occupied,
1148	                            cur_checking | {current.robot_id},
1149	                            cur_blocked_path,
1150	                            None,
1151	                        )
1152	                    )
1153	                    continue
1154	                resume = (
1155	                    self._side_exit_cells(
1156	                        current, task, cur_occupied, reserved, cur_blocked_path
1157	                    )
1158	                    if task is not None
1159	                    else iter(())
1160	                )
1161	            if task is None:
1162	                # A taskless robot that still drives a remaining route never
1163	                # sidesteps off it -- not even to unblock a requester -- so a side
1164	                # cell cannot count as a way out for it.
1165	                continue
1166	            # Otherwise the task-bound blocker might sidestep onto a free side
1167	            # cell itself, but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has
1168	            # to use -- parking there only moves the blockage.
1169	            chained = False
1170	            for side_cell, route in resume:
1171	                if not route or route[0] != current.position:
1172	                    # A genuine exit: the robot drives on elsewhere instead of
1173	                    # returning onto the cell it just vacated.
1174	                    return True
1175	                # The replanned route leads straight back through the cell
1176	                # being vacated. That still counts as leaving when the way
1177	                # back is clear, or when whoever holds it can clear out in
1178	                # turn -- but not when the robot would re-face a jam that has
1179	                # no exit of its own, because then the side step is undone on
1180	                # the next tick with nothing gained.
1181	                hyp_occupied = dict(cur_occupied)
1182	                del hyp_occupied[current.position]
1183	                hyp_occupied[side_cell] = current.robot_id
1184	                holder_id: str | None = None
1185	                for cell in route[1:]:
1186	                    holder = hyp_occupied.get(cell) or reserved.get(cell)
1187	                    if holder is not None and holder != current.robot_id:
1188	                        holder_id = holder
1189	                        break
1190	                if holder_id is None:
1191	                    return True
1192	                if holder_id in cur_checking:
1193	                    continue
1194	                stack.append(
1195	                    (current, cur_occupied, cur_checking, cur_blocked_path, resume)
1196	                )
1197	                stack.append(
1198	                    (
1199	                        self.robots[holder_id],
1200	                        hyp_occupied,
1201	                        cur_checking | {current.robot_id},
1202	                        frozenset(route),
1203	                        None,
1204	                    )
1205	                )
1206	                chained = True
1207	                break
1208	            if chained:
1209	                continue
1210	        return False

1212	    def _update_traffic_waits(
1213	        self,
1214	        waited: dict[str, str],
1215	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
1216	    ) -> None:
1217	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
1218	
1219	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
1220	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
1221	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
1222	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
1223	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
1224	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
1225	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
1226	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
1227	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
1228	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
1229	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
1230	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
1231	        """
1232	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1233	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
1234	        for robot_id in waited:
1235	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
1236	                continue
1237	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
1238	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
1239	                continue
1240	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
1241	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1242	                continue
1243	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
1244	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
1245	                continue
1246	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
1247	            if entry is None:
1248	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
1249	            else:
1250	                surviving[robot_id] = {
1251	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
1252	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
1253	                }
1254	        self._traffic_waits = surviving

1256	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
1257	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
1258	
1259	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
1260	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
1261	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
1262	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
1263	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
1264	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
1265	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
1266	        """
1267	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1268	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
1269	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
1270	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
1271	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
1272	                continue
1273	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
1274	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]

1279	                "robot_id": robot_id,

1281	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
1282	            }
1283	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())

1290	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
1291	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest available robot using stable tie breaks.
1292	
1293	        Only a robot with no bound task *and* no remaining route is available:
1294	        a taskless robot still driving a preset route keeps that route and is
1295	        never selected, even when it is the closest to the pickup -- being
1296	        temporarily blocked by traffic does not count as having finished the
1297	        route either. Skipping such a robot never touches its position,
1298	        mileage, cargo state or remaining waypoints, and never makes other
1299	        tasks wait: the next available robot is chosen by the usual shortest
1300	        feasible route length with the robot id string as tie break.
1301	        """
1302	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
1303	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
1304	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
1305	            for robot in self.robots.values():
1306	                if not robot.idle or robot.route:
1307	                    continue
1308	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
1309	                if route is None:
1310	                    continue
1311	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
1312	            if not choices:
1313	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
1314	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
1315	                continue
1316	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
1317	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
1318	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
1319	            robot.route = route
1320	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
1321	
1322	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
1323	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
1324	        for robot in self.robots.values():
1325	            if robot.task_id is None:
1326	                continue
1327	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
1328	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
1329	                task.picked_up = True

1331	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
1332	        self._confirm_pickups()
1333	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
1334	        self.assign_tasks()
1335	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
1336	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
1337	        self._confirm_pickups()
1338	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1339	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
1340	        moved: list[str] = []
1341	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
1342	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
1343	
1344	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
1345	            del occupied[robot.position]
1346	            robot.position = destination
1347	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
1348	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
1349	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
1350	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
1351	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
1352	
1353	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
1354	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
1355	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
1356	                continue
1357	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
1358	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1359	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
1360	                continue
1361	            if not robot.route:
1362	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1363	                continue
1364	            destination = robot.route[0]
1365	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
1366	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
1367	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
1368	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
1369	                    if route is None:
1370	                        robot.route = []
1371	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
1372	                    else:
1373	                        robot.route = route
1374	                continue
1375	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
1376	            if blocker_id is None:
1377	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
1378	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
1379	                relocate(robot, destination)
1380	                robot.route.pop(0)
1381	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1382	                continue
1383	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
1384	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
1385	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
1386	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:
1387	                if blocker.task_id is None and not blocker.route:
1388	                    # Truly parked blocker: no bound task and no remaining
1389	                    # route. Ask it to yield onto a free side cell, then take
1390	                    # over the cell it vacated. A taskless robot that still has
1391	                    # a remaining route is not parked: it drives that route
